COORDINATOR RULING (owner=user writes; applies to every difficulty, given to reworkers and auditors alike):
Every tree needs one write that is the customer's own. In a school district's family-services desk, an owner=user write is accepted when, and only when, it is an act only the parent or guardian can perform on the spot in real practice:
 (a) a by:user lifecycle transition of the base charter, together with the same-category consequence its base triggers/policies book, with the deviation declared. Examples: the family's written withdrawal notice from Extended Day, accepting an offered waitlist seat or a transfer placement, the family's own cancellation of a permit or registration.
 (b) a payment the parent completes personally through the district's online payment portal or at the campus cashier, after the agent quotes the amount. PCI DSS practice: district staff never take card numbers by phone. The extended policy's own rule states that this payment is the parent's own act, declared as a scoped overwrite wherever a base rule sentence assigns that posting to staff. The persona makes the necessity visible (e.g. "I'll pay it online right now").
 (c) the parent's own deposit of their own funds (e.g. into a meal account).
 (d) a submission that law or district policy requires the parent or guardian to make or sign personally, with the persona making it explicit. Examples: a household meal benefit application, which USDA requires an adult household member to sign; a transfer request; a fee-waiver request; a transportation application.
Not accepted: a label-only owner=user on a posting staff could make without the parent's action, i.e. one with no in-person necessity.
